hints.L0: Think about how to instantiate a module and connect its ports by name when the port order differs from the parent module.
hints.L3: Write each connection as .port(signal), for example .in1(a). With named connections the order inside the parentheses no longer matters.

common_mistakes: Connecting ports by position instead of by name, which fails because mod_a declares outputs before inputs.
Swapping the mapping of a,b,c,d to in1,in2,in3,in4 (e.g., connecting a to in2 and b to in1).
Forgetting to connect one of the inputs or outputs, leaving it floating.
Using the wrong instance name or module name in the instantiation.
top: module top_module(input a, input b, input c, input d, output out1, output out2)
review_notes: Spec: added the required a-d to in1-in4 mapping, which was only in L3. L3: now about named-connection syntax.
